Already before we bought the land I have been thinking about how to partition it.

In our current society government community planners do this (often poorly) however under our laws a private developer has to do it - at least if he wants to sell properties to happy customers.

The plan at the moment is to subdivide the area using a hexagon grid with side lengths of 15m. Each such hexagon would have an area of ~580m².

The main benefit of a hexagonal grid is that you can save on roads, utilities and have roads in every direction. (This sounds fairly obvious, but apparently usual hexagonal plans place roads along the edges like this. I don't know if I'm a genius for noticing you can create straight roads or if people are retarded... and if you think that is bad you should know that public planners favor dead-end cul-de-sac designs, don't ask me why.)

Certain areas would be reserved for road and access use. In other words they would be sold under a conditional contract to a private road company or possibly managed by the neighboring properties.

Main roads would be made up of segments 19 hexagons long (~490m) which form large triangles with points creating 6 way intersections/roundabouts. These main roads using full hexagon segments would have 2 lanes in each direction 3m wide and 2 side walks each 1.5m wide.

To access hexagons away from the main roads one-way streets would be created between every second hexagon row such that one of each hexagon's tips/teeth/corners is "flattened". This would be a one lane and one side walk road with all parking done on private properties. This uses up only ~58m² of the 580m² property.

Further I will split up the resulting 521m² "property hexagons" into two halves because 260m² is sufficient for a small family home with a small garden. People would be free to buy more than one of course.

Furthermore the contracts for the small access roads will be written so that if the entire row is owned by a person or company they may use it as they wish. The contracts for the main roads will be written so that temporary uses such as say farming will be allowed if a road is not needed there at the moment.

Property hexagons would be sold under entirely open contracts except for normal Emergency Nation rules and any rule 8 considerations.

The resulting layout should allow easily scaling to almost any city size and yet also be very space efficient and compact.
